12.1c — Grid/Symmetry Jam: Build Day 2

Day 2, grid edition: the risky sticky-note first, then exactly one system — a rules engine on the grid, a mirrored opponent, or the visual render. By the end of class, strangers could playtest what exists, and the jam is officially shippable-plus.

Build Day ~50 min

Order of the day (the 10.1c day, tuned for grids):

  1. Sticky note (15 min cap). Grid risks are predictable: pathfinding (DON'T — use straight lines and simple checks), turn-order bugs, or the renderer. Do the risky one now or cut it.
  2. One system (20 min). Pick ONE:
// (a) RULES: what a cell does when entered
if (grid[ny, nx] == WALL)  { /* blocked — don't move */ }
if (grid[ny, nx] == HAZZARD) { Lose(); }
if (grid[ny, nx] == EXIT)  { Win(); }

// (b) MIRRORED OPPONENT: the symmetry becomes a player 2/AI
if (grid[ay, ax] == grid[py, px] cell)  // same cell — who rules?
{
    // symmetric collision rule — heads up: DEFINE IT
}

// (c) RENDER: cells to sprites, index → world position
Instantiate(cellPrefab, new Vector3(col * 1f, row * -1f, 0), ...);

Note the (c) trap: row 0 is at the TOP of a text grid but your Unity y-axis points UP — the * -1f flips the board, and this one sign decides whether your game is readable or upside down.

Playtest smoke (10 min). Two minutes with a non-teammate. Watch them MOVE: do they understand the grid instantly, or fight it? Grid games are read in one glance or never.

Close of Day ~5 min

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Resolve the sticky risk inside the cap (or cut it, saying which)
  • Show one rules/collision/render system complete
  • Explain your symmetry's tie/deadlock rule in a sentence
  • Declare shippable with the wishlist ranked
